newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends steady, traders await API data.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends steady, traders await API data.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended near unchanged, erasing earlier gains but recovering from a weak barge trade that undercut the market for the second day in a row, traders said on Tuesday.
Traders waited for the American Petroleum Institute data due out later today, after last week's report showed a steep drop of 3.8 million barrels in U.S. gasoline supplies.
U.S. traders said they expected gasoline stocks to rose 0.10 million barrels from the current 186.0 million.
A slight bounce in Brent crude prices aided gasoline but Brent soon pulled back to show only modest gains.
Continued buying into the U.K. ahead of the government's November 26 budget was still cited as a prop for NWE prices, while clouding the exact spreads between prompt and end-of-the-month prices.
"It is a crystal ball," said one trader, referring to what will happen at the end of the month.

Stockbuilding ahead of the budget has led to a premium for prompt prices that may encourage refiners to sell, she said. But any sharp price selloff after the budget could open the arbitrage to the U.S. that would indirectly support European prices, she said.
The arbitrage to the U.S. from northwest Europe is now shut, she said.
Eurograde barges gained as much as $3 to trade at $228 fob Rotterdam refinery material, then dipped to a late trade at $222.25 fob ARA, traders said.
But bids quickly perked back up to about $224, unchanged from yesterday, they said.
Regular unleaded barges continued to trade thinly and hold about an $8 discount to premium unleaded.
Premium unleaded cargoes were steady at $230 cif.
